aspects.says: Every write to a CopyOnWriteArrayList copies the whole array, so time and allocation per write grow with the list's size.
basis: section:Every Copy-on-Write Write Copies the Whole Array, So Its Cost Grows with the List

aspects.says: A fail-fast collection fits data one thread owns, where its exception reports a bug in the loop.
basis: section:Once Another Thread Writes, a Fail-Fast Walk Fails at Random; a Small Listener List Needs a Snapshot
aspects.reason: a one-clause pointer to unit 6.5.3, whose practices check the in-loop bug

aspects.says: CopyOnWriteArrayList.set skips the copy when the new element is the same object as the old one, which can distort a measurement.
basis: section:Every Copy-on-Write Write Copies the Whole Array, So Its Cost Grows with the List
aspects.reason: a benchmarking detail of the page's own measurement; no graded behaviour depends on it

aspects.says: Once another thread writes, a walk over a fail-fast collection fails at random, not only with ConcurrentModificationException, and often after it has already handled some elements, so retrying it repeats them.
basis: section:Once Another Thread Writes, a Fail-Fast Walk Fails at Random; a Small Listener List Needs a Snapshot

aspects.says: A snapshot charges each write a copy of the whole map, so it fits small or rarely written data; a lock makes writers wait out each read, which suits large, busy data.
basis: section:A Total That Must Add Up Needs a Snapshot or a Lock, and Size Decides Which

aspects.says: A small list that threads share, read far more often than it is written, fits CopyOnWriteArrayList: a walk never fails and takes no lock, so a write never waits for it.
basis: section:Once Another Thread Writes, a Fail-Fast Walk Fails at Random; a Small Listener List Needs a Snapshot

aspects.says: A mutable map kept in an AtomicReference and changed in place is not a snapshot: a reader walks the live map.
basis: section:A Total That Must Add Up Needs a Snapshot or a Lock, and Size Decides Which

aspects.says: A read that must agree across elements needs a snapshot published whole or a lock held by writers and the reader alike.
basis: section:A Total That Must Add Up Needs a Snapshot or a Lock, and Size Decides Which

aspects.says: A weakly consistent walk fits work that handles each element on its own: it takes no lock, never fails, and writers go on during it.
basis: section:A Weakly Consistent Walk Fits Work on One Element at a Time, Not a Total Across Elements

aspects.says: A total added up by a weakly consistent walk while writers move value between keys can be one the collection never held, even though each update is atomic.
basis: section:A Weakly Consistent Walk Fits Work on One Element at a Time, Not a Total Across Elements
